meta.subtitle: BH6CAZ — a handheld on the balcony, listening from Hefei.

intro: Amateur radio is the hobby that taught me the most for the least money. My station is modest — a handheld, a roll-up antenna, and a habit of going outside when the weather is good — but on a quiet evening I can still reach repeaters across the city and occasionally catch a station far beyond it. I mostly work VHF and UHF, I am slowly learning Morse code, and I am always happy to answer a call from another operator, especially someone who is also just starting out.

facts.label: Rig
facts.value: Baofeng UV-5R Mini — a transparent handheld that is easy to carry and looks great.

qsl.title: QSL Cards
qsl.note: I answer every card I receive, and I am glad to send one to anyone who has heard me on the air. Direct requests are the fastest: include your own callsign, the date and time of our contact, the band or repeater you used, and a self-addressed envelope if you would like a paper card back. If you would rather not use the post, an email with a confirmation request is perfectly fine — and if we have already confirmed through a logging service, that counts too.

cards.label: QSL via QRZ
cards.tip: My QRZ profile lists the current confirmation details and the address to use for direct paper cards.

cards.label: Request by Email
cards.tip: Send me the details of our contact and I will reply with a confirmation or a card, whichever you would like.

qrz.text: Look up BH6CAZ on QRZ for my full station details and confirmation history.
